## In one sentence

Community ecology asks how species interactions and the environment shape the
composition, abundance, and diversity of assemblages.

## Core interactions

- Competition occurs when organisms use a limiting shared resource.
- Predation includes consumption of animals; herbivory is consumption of plants or algae.
- Mutualism benefits both partners, while parasitism benefits one and harms the other.
- Facilitation occurs when one species improves conditions for another.

Interactions depend on context. The same species pair can compete in one season
and facilitate one another in another environment.

## Food webs and indirect effects

Food webs represent many feeding links rather than a single linear chain. A
change in one species can affect others indirectly through shared predators,
prey, or resources. A trophic cascade is a strong top-down effect that travels
across multiple trophic levels.

## Diversity and succession

Species richness is the number of species. Evenness describes how balanced their
abundances are. Succession describes changes in community composition through
time after colonisation or disturbance. There is no single universal endpoint:
disturbance regime, climate, dispersal, and species interactions all matter.

::: {.callout-important}
Do not treat diversity as one number. State whether you mean richness, evenness,
functional diversity, or phylogenetic diversity, and define the sampling unit.
:::

## Check your understanding

Draw a three-level food web and remove its top predator. Predict two direct and
two indirect changes, then identify an observation that would test your prediction.
